{{MedalBronze| [[Basketball at the 2001 Summer Universiade|2001 Beijing]] | [[United States national basketball team|Team competition]]}} }} '''Lonny Leroy Baxter''' (born January 27, 1979) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He is {{height|ft=6|in=8}} in height, and played the [[power forward]] and [[center (basketball)|center]] positions. ==College career== While attending the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], Baxter won the 2002 [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|championship]] along with teammates and future [[NBA]] players [[Juan Dixon]], [[Steve Blake]] and [[Chris Wilcox]] by defeating [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]]. He was named a regional MVP of the NCAA Tournament twice, in 2001 and 2002.{{Citation needed|date=December 2013}} ==Professional career== === NBA === Baxter was selected by the [[Chicago Bulls]] with the 15th pick of the second round (44th overall) of the [[2002 NBA draft]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2002/board/index.html |title=NBA Draft Board |work=nba.com |access-date=2011-01-29}} On February 9, 2006, Baxter was traded by the [[Houston Rockets]] to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] for [[Keith Bogans]]. Baxter's final game was played on April 19, 2006, in a 96–86 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] where he played for 7 minutes and the only stat he recorded was 1 rebound. Baxter has career NBA averages of 3.9 points and 2.9 rebounds in 162 total games from 2002 to 2006. ===Europe=== During the 2004–05 season Baxter played some games for the [[A1 Ethniki|Greek A1 League]] team [[Panathinaikos BC|Panathinaikos]], before getting injured and agreeing with the club for his release. On August 8, 2006, Baxter signed with the [[Serie A (basketball)|Italian League]] team [[Montepaschi Siena]]. In 2008, he joined [[Panionios BC|Panionios]]. In 2009, he moved to [[Beşiktaş Cola Turka]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.turkbasket.com/haber/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=4293:kartal-bombay-patlatt&catid=94:bjk-colaturka&Itemid=279|title=Beşiktaş'a süper pivot|date=July 12, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090712123643/http://www.turkbasket.com/haber/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=4293:kartal-bombay-patlatt&catid=94:bjk-colaturka&Itemid=279 |archive-date=2009-07-12 }} ==Personal life== On August 16, 2006, Baxter was arrested in [[Washington, D.C.]], only a few blocks from the [[White House]] after firing a .40 caliber [[Glock]] handgun into the air.{{cite news | title=Baxter's prospects in Italy uncertain after sentencing | url=https://www.espn.co.uk/nba/news/story?id=2559851 | publisher=Associated Press | via=ESPN | date=24 August 2006 | accessdate=5 August 2025}} On August 23, 2006, Baxter was sentenced to 60 days in prison after pleading guilty to possession of an unregistered firearm and unregistered ammunition charges. DC Superior Court judge Craig Iscoe said:{{cite news | title=Former Raptor Lonny Baxter pleads guilty to gun charge | url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/former-raptor-lonny-baxter-pleads-guilty-to-gun-charge-1.624884 | website=[[CBC Sports]] | date=23 August 2006 | accessdate=5 August 2025 }} {{blockquote|There's no good reason for a person who's not working in law enforcement or presidential protection to be in possession of a loaded weapon within blocks of the White House, let alone to fire it into the air}} Baxter was later charged with shipping four guns via [[FedEx]] in July 2006 without notifying them that the shipment contained firearms. Baxter [[plea bargain|pled guilty]] to this crime on July 19, 2007.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportsline.com/collegebasketball/story/10261990|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070823065823/http://sportsline.com/collegebasketball/story/10261990|url-status=dead|title=Ex-Terp, former Bull Baxter pleads guilty to illegally shipping guns.|archivedate=August 23, 2007}} He was sentenced to 60 days in jail, two years of supervised release and a $2,000 fine on August 31,
